Your room

🛏️ What's included in the Bungalow

The headline feature

The sliding door splits the room into two separate sleeping zones — real separation over 14 nights, not one open room.

Standard inclusions

Air-con, minibar, kettle, in-room safe, hairdryer, satellite TV, telephone, private bathroom with shower, balcony or terrace, daily housekeeping with towel swap, bottled water/fruit topped up in-room. Free WiFi resort-wide.

Location in the resort

📍 Best place to be — and what to ask for

  • Block C or D: the sweet spot — sits between the main reception/Aqua Park North cluster and the Aqua Park South/Midway area, so neither end of the resort is a long walk.
  • Block A: closest to reception (Rooms 1001–1122) if a short check-in walk matters more than being mid-resort — but also the busiest/noisiest, being right by the main hub.
  • Ask for: "somewhere central, please — just not right on the entertainment stage." That's the one spot guests consistently flag as noisy late into the night.

The bars

Jungle Bar, Red Sky Bar, White Elephant Bar, Columbus Bar, Jazz Bar and Lobby Bar are the named ones that come up again and again in reviews — 12 in total scattered round the resort. All are on the Map tab; filter to "Bars" to see them at a glance.

A la carte spots sometimes need a same-day table booking via reception — ask what the system is on day one.
The beach

🏖️ Getting sand between your toes

  • Neverland's beach access is at a sister resort across the main road — not walkable, reached by a free shuttle.
  • Reported frequency is roughly every 20–30 minutes, no fixed timetable, about 5–15 minutes each way.
  • Coarse, "builders'-sand" rather than soft golden sand — worth setting expectations, especially for little feet.
  • Sunbeds and umbrellas are provided, and guests consistently rate the snorkelling well.
  • Bring your pool towel card/towel with you on the shuttle — you currently can't swap for a fresh one at the beach itself.
Best treated as a half-day trip rather than a full-day base, given the shuttle gaps.
Getting around the resort

🧭 Walking, shuttles, buggies and bikes

🚶 Walking (the default)

The resort is genuinely huge — "it's a bit of a walk if you're on the wrong side" is one of the most repeated lines in reviews. Expect serious step counts most days; comfortable shoes matter more than any shuttle timetable.

🚌 Internal shuttle / buggy

A free shuttle loops the grounds, but timing is inconsistent — guests report anywhere from every 15 to every 30 minutes with no published timetable. Treat it as a bonus if one turns up, not something to plan your day around.

🏖️ Beach shuttle

Separate service specifically to the sister beach resort — roughly every 20–30 minutes, 5–15 minutes each way. See the Beach section above.

🚲 Family pedal bikes

Free 4-person bikes, station near the Ice Rink, good for lapping the resort. Nominally 30 minutes but not strictly timed in practice. Drop them back at the station rather than assuming you can park one overnight at your bungalow.

🚕 Beyond the resort

Senzo Mall is roughly a 10–15 minute walk, or a couple of minutes by taxi. Uber/taxis can collect from the main entrance — show your wristbands at the gate for drop-offs. Your airport transfer is already a shared coach, booked as part of the package.

Use the Map tab's route planner — and the walking-time table on that tab — for exact-ish timings between any two points.
Beyond the resort

🚌 Excursions — what's worth it, and what to book where

The three excursions that come up again and again for Hurghada: a boat trip out to Orange Bay/Giftun Island, a desert safari, and a day trip to Luxor. None of these are run by Neverland itself, so how you book them matters.

Book through a known platform or the resort desk — not a street seller

GetYourGuide and Viator are the two big international booking platforms guests use for Egypt excursions — both show real review counts, have free cancellation on most listings, and give you somewhere to complain if a trip doesn't deliver. The resort's own excursions desk is the other safe route. Guests consistently warn about persistent independent sellers around the resort and in town — same advice as the Guest Tips section: book official, not off a stranger's badge.

🐠 Orange Bay / Giftun Island snorkelling boat trip

Full day, roughly 8am–4pm. Boat out to Giftun Island's national park, 2–3 snorkel stops, lunch and soft drinks on board included. Listed from around €19–25pp on GetYourGuide/Viator, though "VIP" or smaller-boat versions run higher. Watch for: the Giftun Island National Park entry fee (~€10pp) is often paid separately, in cash, on the day — not always included in the headline price.

Example listing — Viator

🏜️ Desert safari (quad bike, Bedouin village, BBQ & show)

Evening versions (quad/buggy ride, Bedouin village, camel ride, BBQ dinner, tanoura show) run roughly $20–40pp; full-day "super safari" versions around $25–40pp. Genuinely popular with kids for the camels and the show. Watch for: a few reviews flag the cheapest listings as very short on actual quad-bike time ("10 minutes on the quad, 10 minutes in the car") — check recent reviews for ride duration, not just the price tag, before booking.

Example listing — Viator

🏛️ Luxor day trip (Valley of the Kings, Karnak, Hatshepsut Temple)

By road: roughly 3–3.5 hours each way across the Eastern Desert, full day out from around €55–65pp including lunch and a guide. By domestic flight instead: a ~45-minute EgyptAir hop each way (roughly $50–80 one-way) buys back several hours of actual site time versus the drive.

Prices above are illustrative ranges pulled from current listings, not a quote — always check the live price, inclusions, and cancellation terms on the platform before booking.
Towels

🩴 Do you need to bring or buy pool towels?

No — don't pack or budget for beach towels.

  • In the room: plenty of towels for showering, swapped daily by housekeeping.
  • For the pools: at check-in you're each given a towel card, exchanged at towel huts round the resort — swap again anytime for a fresh one.
  • A few recent reviews mention a card-free "swap dirty for clean" trial instead. Either way, you won't need your own.
Water slides

🌊 Height and weight rules

Minimum height

Most big slides sit between 110cm and 140cm minimum height depending on the ride, strictly enforced — a marked ruler and staff member check every rider.

Weight

No published blanket weight limit — a handful of bigger thrill slides may post their own individual limit.

Younger kids

The dedicated Kids Aqua Park has shallow pools, splash pads and mini-slides with no height bar at all.

If either of the kids is borderline, worth measuring them before you fly — 120cm is roughly the line for most "big" slides.
Fairground / Midway

🎡 Rides, hours, and restrictions

  • How many: around a dozen rides — Ferris wheel, dodgems, smaller kiddie rides — all free, next to a bar and stage with nightly entertainment.
  • Hours: officially ~8–10pm, but recent guests report it running later through the week (10:30, 11, even 11:30pm).
  • Height/weight: no published master list — each ride has its own posted marker. Dodgems reportedly carry a roughly 90kg rider weight limit.
  • Popcorn, candy floss and dough balls handed out free most evenings.
What guests all agree on

💡 Patterns from recent reviews & forums

Not one-off gripes — these keep coming up independently across reviews from the last couple of years.

🛏️ Sunbeds: go early

Officially no reserving; in practice, people do — especially the soft four-poster beds. Several guests mention one adult heading over before breakfast to claim one.

💶 Tipping isn't pushed here

Compared with some other Egyptian resorts, staff aren't chasing tips — service felt genuine. Small EGP notes in the bar tip jars are still appreciated.

🍦 Ice cream: evenings only

Recent guests report ice cream roughly 7–9pm rather than all day as in previous years.

🌊 Early afternoon = water buggies in the main pool

Part of the main activity pool is given over to water buggies roughly 1–3pm most days, shrinking swim space.

🐈 Resort cats — be kind, don't overfeed

Friendly strays roam the grounds, looked after by a volunteer welfare group (reception can give you their contact). Guests love them, but it's best to stick to what the group recommends rather than free-feeding.

🗺️ Get your bearings on day one

The single most repeated advice: it's overwhelming at first, and everyone says they "found their bearings" after a day or so. The Map tab is built for exactly that.

🎟️ Watch for persistent excursion sellers

Guests consistently mention being approached about external trips around the resort — book through the official excursions desk for proper protection.

🧺 Towel art is a genuine highlight

Multiple reviews mention housekeeping leaving daily "towel art" animals in the room — a small thing that keeps getting a mention as a kids' favourite.

🕑 Check-in / check-out

Generally reported as check-in from 14:00, check-out by 12:00 — worth confirming, and asking about bag storage if you land and want to hit the pool straight away.

For scale

📐 How big is Neverland, really?

Both real resort maps, drawn to true relative scale and centred on the same point. Fade Center Parcs in and out to see how much of it Neverland would actually fill.

~100,000m²Neverland's built footprint (10 hectares)
400 acresCenter Parcs Longford (≈1.62 million m²)
~16x biggerCenter Parcs' land area vs Neverland's

The catch: Center Parcs' 400 acres is mostly forest, with lodges spread through the trees — you cycle everywhere. Neverland's 10 hectares is almost entirely built: pools, slides and buildings wall-to-wall. Expect far more walking density packed into a much smaller space here than at Center Parcs.

70%

Both maps are the real, official resort maps (Pickalbatros's and Center Parcs' own), scaled by their true published areas — 400 acres and ~100,000m² — and centred on the same point, not GPS-aligned to real-world position.

Money

💶 Quick cash reference

  • Egyptian Pounds (EGP) cover tips and small extras — smaller notes are more useful than big ones at bars and towel huts.
  • A currency exchange desk and ATM are on site near reception (marked on the Map tab) — worth a glance at the logo on it, for the reason below.
  • Cards work for anything formal or resort-billed; cash keeps the small stuff moving quickly.

Which ATMs to actually use

Stick to National Bank of Egypt (NBE), Banque Misr, CIB (Commercial International Bank), or QNB Alahli — the four consistently recommended for foreign cards, with standalone machines in bazaars and unbranded kiosks the ones more likely to get skimmed. Always decline "Dynamic Currency Conversion" and pay in EGP, not your home currency.

The on-site machine isn't confirmed to any specific bank, so it's worth checking the logo when you get there. Senzo Mall is a safer bet if it turns out to be an independent operator — a guest there confirmed using both NBE and CIB machines with no issues.

Extra tips

✨ A few more things worth knowing

  • Book the dinner show early: the once-per-stay free Neverland Dinner Show is worth booking at reception on day one — 4–5 day waits for a slot aren't unusual.
  • Passport & visa: passports need 6 months' validity beyond travel (past mid-March 2027), and everyone — including Olivia and Loughlann — needs a tourist visa.
  • Airport transfer, realistically: Neverland is genuinely close to the airport (~10km, ~17 minutes direct), but the included easyJet holidays coach stops at other resorts on the way. Expect something in the 1–2 hour bracket door to door, not 20 minutes — just part of arrival day, not a problem with your booking.
